decisions: Cross-language projects are architecture, algorithm and challenge sources; end-to-end absolute performance claims are limited to semantically comparable Apple-platform implementations.
The comparison system is divided into platform baselines, portable mechanisms, client pipelines and adjacent systems.
Native upstream tests are preserved and reported independently from Fovea semantic challenge tests.
Every implemented Fovea capability must be first or statistically equivalent to the best eligible comparator on all preregistered primary endpoints; capability gaps remain explicit.
The canonical end-to-end and specialty workload matrix contains W1 through W15 and completion of W1-W3 never implies completion of the matrix.

The mandatory A-tier unified Apple-platform matrix is Apple URLSession + ImageIO, Apple AsyncImage, Nuke, Kingfisher, SDWebImage, PINRemoteImage, and Fovea; AlamofireImage is retained as B-tier evidence and cannot substitute for an A-tier entry.
openItems: Complete the missing Apple URLSession + ImageIO, Apple AsyncImage, and PINRemoteImage integrations before treating the direct matrix as complete.
Implement and activate dedicated plans for W4-W15 in dependency order.
Add Apple native baselines and PINRemoteImage to eligible direct matrices when locked and adapted.
Complete stable-iOS and lower-performance physical-device replication.

decisions: Hard correctness and security invariants precede all performance claims.
Semantic comparability is a requirement-relative partial order, not an unqualified equality check.
All metric directions are normalized to loss before non-inferiority, equivalence or superiority decisions.
Equivalence requires preregistered margins and TOST or an equivalent confidence-interval criterion; failure to reject difference is not equivalence.
Multiplicity correction is applied inside preregistered claim families.
Dependent trace observations use run or block level resampling; DKW is restricted to justified independent samples.
Distribution diagnostics may include ECDF dominance violations and Wasserstein distance, but do not replace primary claim-family decisions.
EVT remains research-only until threshold selection, dependence and model validation are preregistered.
Cache evaluation includes delayed-hit aggregate waiting, not only Belady hit-rate regret.
Global unbounded world-best claims are forbidden; only evidence-bound best-within-scope or weaker certificates are machine generated.
openItems: Add claim families only before the corresponding formal data are observed.
Implement runtime history refinement or linearizability checking for W6 and W7.
Evaluate LIRS, GDSF and size-aware algorithms as research baselines without pre-committing production replacement.

entries.incident: The active repository retained only W1-W4, while the earlier accepted W1-W15 matrix survived only in user-provided discussion material. Subsequent work over-focused on W1-W3 and incorrectly reconstructed W4-W15.
openItems: Keep the continuity, workload, source and unresolved-obligation gates active in local verification and CI.
Any future accepted discussion that changes long-term scope must be normalized into the ledger before task completion.
remediation: Restore W1-W15 from the retained discussion source and record its digest.
Create a machine-readable project memory and discussion ledger.
Require a pre-task continuity bootstrap before repository changes.
Add memory, source, workload and unresolved-obligation gates to verify.sh and CI.
Make supersession explicit and forbid silent deletion or renumbering of accepted workloads.
rootCauses: No mandatory session bootstrap loaded active decisions and unresolved obligations.
No gate required the workload catalog to remain gap-free W1-W15.
Conversation summaries were treated as sufficient continuity evidence.
The current phase subset was not visibly separated from the full roadmap.

decisions: Fovea and the independent codec advance in parallel; neither project waits for the other to complete.
The integration boundary is a versioned finite capability/resource/lifecycle contract, not direct dependence on codec internals.
ImageIO remains the conservative reference backend until a candidate passes a shared cross-repository conformance kit and bounded rollout evidence.
Progressive, animation, HDR and output-representation types do not close W4/W5/W9 capability gaps without production pipeline and workload evidence.
Claims of being stronger than ImageIO or libjpeg-turbo must be decomposed by format, correctness, safety, quality, latency, throughput, memory, energy and feature scope.
Current literature informs contract and experimental lanes, but learned/generative codec mechanisms do not enter Fovea public API without an implemented backend and evidence.
openItems: Run ImageCodec conformance v1 against the independent codec once it exposes ImageCraft contract v1; the ImageIO self-host fixture passes all six obligations.
Add hostile-corpus, fuzz, sanitizer and resource/lifecycle evidence before any Fovea default-selection claim.
Implement W4 progressive delivery, W5 animation and HDR/output surfaces only through separate ADRs and workload gates.
Preserve immediate ImageIO fallback and prohibit default selection before shadow/canary/physical-device evidence.

decisions: ImageCraft and Akashic are independent package/repository boundaries; Fovea remains the owner of network, HTTP, authorization, identity, namespace revoke, shared-work and cross-store commit semantics.
ImageCraft already exists as an independent local package, so the next codec task is release qualification and current exact-pin Fovea integration rather than recreating an ImageIO wrapper.
Akashic is domain-neutral at its current public boundary; Fovea-specific OriginalEncoded, ContentID, HTTP representation and account/logout semantics must not become Akashic public API.

Fovea keeps a safe ImageIO plus Akashic default composition while advanced callers may inject codec, rendered-memory cache and qualified persistent-store implementations at explicit composition boundaries.
Global mutable registries, arbitrary post-key request mutation and plugin control over alias, shared-task, namespace-generation or commit-coordination state remain forbidden.

Competitive success is defined by scoped semantic-equivalence classes: hard invariants first, non-inferiority on every preregistered primary endpoint, and superiority on at least one endpoint, with gaps and non-comparability preserved.
Future cross-platform work first shares contracts, fixtures, traces and evidence; runtime portability is introduced only when a real non-Apple implementation proves the abstraction.
openItems: Run provider and codec v1 kits against real independent implementations.
Complete physical-device resource, energy and Akashic power-loss evidence.
Repeat W3/W8/W13 and final comparisons on clean current source and stable physical devices.

decisions: The P0-P9 long-horizon route skeleton is mandatory repository context for every multi-step Fovea task and must not depend on chat memory.
Every task must map its work to a roadmap phase and an open obligation; unfinished phases and blocked queue items remain visible across sessions.
Phase removal, renumbering or material sequencing changes require explicit discussion-ledger supersession rather than silent plan rewriting.
The roadmap control plane is machine-readable and validated by the existing project-memory gate so local verification and CI fail when it drifts or disappears.
Execution begins immediately with P0 baseline capture and decode-resource contract audit while current exact-pin evidence remains bound to explicit source identity.
Research repositories inform adoption, rejection and experiment-only decisions, but they do not become Fovea runtime dependencies merely because they exist.
openItems: Publish a privacy-sanitized Fovea root commit and establish protected public CI.
Resolve the decode working-set coverage ambiguity or retain the fail-closed resource policy before a second production codec.
Run the current codec and storage conformance kits against real independent implementations.
Complete physical-device resource, energy and power-loss evidence.

decisions: ImageCraft and Akashic already satisfy the local logical-extraction objective; the immediate objective is release-grade physical dependency migration, not recreating wrappers.
ImageCraft and Akashic public exact revisions are now the sole production component sources; embedded mirrors and source-lock governance are retired.
ImageCodec is the only accepted codec composition contract; arbitrary ImageDecoding compatibility paths are removed.

Persistent cache substitution must be expressed as an immutable qualified store bundle that preserves generation, writer lifetime, namespace persistence and cross-store transaction obligations; independent raw store hooks are rejected.
Cross-repository validation should use separate minimal codec and storage conformance kits, while component evidence and Fovea composition evidence remain distinct.

The current-stack comparison target is scoped Pareto certification: hard invariants first, non-inferiority on all preregistered primary endpoints and superiority on at least one endpoint, with gaps and non-comparability retained.

New features and speculative cross-platform runtime abstraction are lower priority than clean source identity, release governance, exact dependency identity, immediate safe fallback, resource evidence and composition correctness.
openItems: Publish the privacy-sanitized Fovea root, observe public CI, protect main and create the first immutable Fovea tag.
Run codec/provider v1 kits against real independent components; both self-host fixtures now pass.
Repeat W1/W2/W3/W7/W8/W10/W13 on protected clean source and stable physical devices.

decisions: Fovea, ImageCraft and Akashic use the MIT License; third-party and public-domain media remain outside the MIT grant and retain per-file provenance.
Public histories are sanitized development histories with GitHub noreply authors; pre-publication histories remain only in local bundles and archive branches and are not pushed.
ImageCraft and Akashic are consumed by public HTTPS URLs and exact full commit revisions recorded in Package.swift, Package.resolved and component-pins.json.
Embedded ImageCraft and Akashic production sources, temporary external-package templates and embedded-source lock gates are retired.
Compiler-warning strictness applies to Fovea-owned sources without overriding external package warning policy.
Superseded narrative reports and extraction provenance are removed, while machine evidence needed to interpret still-valid claims remains immutable.

The 2026-08-01 action direction is the current narrative plan; the superseded 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-30 operational roadmaps are deleted after their durable decisions and completed facts were normalized into machine-readable memory.
openItems: Publish the privacy-sanitized Fovea root, observe public CI, protect main and retain the first immutable Fovea alpha tag.
Complete physical-device resource, energy and physical power-loss evidence.

decisions: Cross-platform inputs are adopted as falsifiable mechanisms and challenge tests, not copied public APIs or runtime dependencies.
Codec and store selection remains build-time immutable and capability-qualified; global mutable registries and implicit singletons remain rejected.
Glide and Fresco inform join-cancel-release and ownership-ledger tests, while Fovea retains a fixed-stage runtime rather than a public producer DAG.
libvips-style region/tile execution remains an internal P8/P9 experiment until a real second backend proves the identity, lifecycle and resource boundary.
Caffeine is an external executable policy oracle only; SIEVE, S3-FIFO, W-TinyLFU and S4-FIFO must use identical traces, capacity models and loss metrics.

Learning-augmented cache or prefetch policy may influence low-frequency control decisions only, must have deterministic fallback, and cannot alter identity, authorization, revoke or persistence eligibility.
openItems: Add join-versus-cancel model checking and resource ownership/reclaim-tail evidence.
Build a fixed-revision external cache-policy replay oracle for W13.
Prototype region/tile execution only after a second real codec backend exists.

decisions: Fovea, ImageCraft, Akashic and every active consumer/benchmark SwiftPM manifest move to tools version 6.4 while retaining iOS 15 and macOS 12 deployment targets.
Every repository fails closed unless Xcode 27 or newer with Apple Swift 6.4 is selected; compiler identity is part of local evidence rather than an ambient assumption.

Fovea adopts async defer for permit/subscription/preparation cleanup and weak let for immutable non-owning relationships; Akashic adopts a noncopyable writer lease acquired through a dedicated serial actor.
Swift Build product paths are discovered through swift build --show-bin-path; scripts may not hard-code .build/debug or .build/out product locations.

RawSpan parser adoption, public noncopyable decode preparation, task cancellation shields, SwiftPM SBOM certification and manual optimizer attributes remain deferred or rejected until deployment, compiler and A/B evidence gates are satisfied.
No performance claim follows from a language-version bump alone; every optimization attribute or hot-loop rewrite requires a named workload, interleaved baseline and code-size/resource review.

GitHub now provides an explicit xcode-27 public-preview runner. macos-26 remains invalid for tools 6.4; component PRs and the Fovea private root must use xcode-27, verify compiler identity, and preserve preview provenance before pins, tags or protected-CI claims advance.

The prior Fovea publication task remains active: the repository stays private because the seventh root exposed an order-sensitive Workbench UI shard failure even though the isolated diagnostic test passed.

The Workbench order-dependent product-patterns failure is locally resolved by test-scoped main-actor application termination; the exact original five-test shard passes 5/5 and isolated retry is no longer used as evidence.
The diagnostics backpressure test now waits for a bounded observable condition instead of fixed scheduling delays; it passes 20/20 and the local three-repository composition passes 475/475.

The full locked comparison infrastructure builds under Swift 6.4: seven macOS adapters, seven iOS adapters and Apple/Fovea SwiftUI surfaces; this is current integration evidence only and phase1DeclarationAllowed remains false.
openItems: Complete the sanitized private Fovea xcode-27 root including native arm64 and Rosetta-backed x86_64 identity vectors and full verification.
Complete physical-device resource/energy and true Akashic power-loss evidence.
Revisit linear ImageCraft preparation, RawSpan and SBOM only when their retained exit conditions are met.
